Local Tastes
Cazuela de Mariscos
Cartagena's definitive dish — a rich Caribbean seafood stew with shrimp, clams, squid, and fish cooked with coconut milk and a sofrito of tomato, onion, and ají dulce. Served in a clay pot at nearly every traditional restaurant.
La Cocina de Pepina · Bocagrande
Arroz con Coco
Toasted coconut rice — the essential Caribbean side dish of the Colombian coast, with a subtle sweetness from the coconut cream that caramelises in the pan. Served alongside grilled fish and cazuela at virtually every coastal restaurant.
Every traditional restaurant in Cartagena
Patacones
Green plantains sliced, smashed flat, and twice-fried until golden and crisp — the Caribbean equivalent of a chip, eaten salted as a snack or as a base for shredded chicken, hogao, and ají picante throughout the old city and Getsemaní.
Street vendors throughout Getsemaní and Bocagrande beach
Limonada de Coco
A blended lemonade made with fresh lime juice, condensed milk, ice, and young coconut flesh — the signature refreshment of Cartagena's beach vendors and open-air bars, best ordered at the Bocagrande beachfront stalls in the afternoon.
Beach vendors · Playa Bocagrande
Sancocho de Gallina
A thick chicken stew with yuca, potato, corn, and cilantro — the Colombian coastal comfort dish eaten for Sunday lunch; the correct accompaniment is white rice and a wedge of lime squeezed at the table.
La Cocina de Pepina · Bocagrande
Food Delivery
Rappi
Foreign number: accepted. — the Rappi app accepts international numbers at signup; SMS verification code arrives on US, Canadian, and European numbers without issue.
The dominant food delivery platform in Colombia; coverage across Bocagrande, Centro Histórico, and Getsemaní is strong with delivery times of 30–50 minutes; selection includes local restaurants, Éxito and Carulla supermarkets, and pharmacy delivery in one app.
rappi.com.co
Uber Eats
Foreign number: accepted. — OTP verification arrives reliably; connect the same account used elsewhere; no Colombia-specific signup required.
Narrower restaurant selection than Rappi in Cartagena but often faster delivery in Bocagrande; strong coverage of chain restaurants and hotel-district cafés; reliable for late-night orders when local kitchens are closed.
ubereats.com

Getting Around
Uber
Foreign number: accepted. — OTP arrives reliably on US, Canadian, and European numbers; use the same account as at home with no additional setup required.
Reliable across Bocagrande, Getsemaní, and the walled city; surge pricing applies during carnival week in February and during cruise-ship days when demand spikes at the port gate; drivers navigate the narrow old-city streets well.
uber.com
InDriver
Foreign number: accepted. — international country-code selector at signup; SMS OTP arrives on foreign numbers; download and register before arrival to save time.
Consistently cheaper than Uber for longer trips to Convento de la Popa, La Boquilla, and Casa Rafael Núñez; the bidding model lets you propose a fare and the driver accepts or counters — typically 20–30% below Uber's quoted price on the same route.
indriver.com
Worth Knowing

Pay in pesos — USD is technically accepted but always costs you more

The Colombian peso — COP — is the only currency that gets you market-rate prices in Cartagena. Street vendors, taxi drivers, and smaller restaurants routinely quote in USD for tourists but apply a 15–25% conversion premium. Withdraw COP at any Bancolombia or Davivienda ATM — both reliably accept foreign cards and charge lower fees than hotel exchanges. Visa and Mastercard work broadly; American Express is hit-or-miss outside luxury hotels.

The walled city and Bocagrande are safe to walk during the day. After dark, Getsemaní is lively on the Plaza de la Trinidad but quieter side streets warrant the same caution you'd give any Latin American city at night — keep valuables out of sight and take Uber rather than walking across the moat. The US State Department rates Colombia Level 2 — Exercise Increased Caution.

The city's main international airport, Rafael Núñez — airport code CTG — is 15 minutes from Bocagrande by Uber — close enough that early departures are low stress. Taxis from outside the terminal are unmetered; agree the fare before you get in or use Uber from the arrivals hall to avoid the negotiation entirely.
